{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against 19 playbook rules. Eleven clauses are compliant, several materially in our favour (IP ownership, assignment and change of control, termination for convenience, audit, governing law, MFN, non-solicitation, renewal, insurance). Eight clauses are deviations, and seven of those sit in walk-away territory under the playbook.

The most serious problems cluster in the risk-allocation and commitment provisions:

- **No Vendor indemnity at all.** § 20 contains only a one-way Customer-to-Vendor indemnity covering "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services", and § 9.3 cross-references infringement remedies in a non-existent "Section 20.5".
- **Liability cap of one month's Fees, "without exception".** § 21.1 sits far below the 12-month fallback (and below the six-month walk-away threshold) and pulls the Excluded Claims in § 21.3 (confidentiality, data protection, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) inside the cap.
- **Commitments and restrictive covenants that fail every fallback term.** A three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" (§ 2.1), sole-and-exclusive sourcing for the full term (§ 2.2), and a 24-month worldwide post-term non-compete (§ 12.4).
- **A revocable, Customer-only Services licence** (§ 13.1) that excludes Affiliates and contractors and contradicts §§ 13.2–13.3.
- **No transition assistance and immediate deletion of Customer Data** (§ 11.1), contradicting §§ 11.2–11.3.

We also note several internal inconsistencies that strengthen our position: § 12.3 records that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete or minimum-volume commitment, which conflicts directly with §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4; and there is no order-of-precedence clause to resolve those conflicts.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 20 (with § 9.3 cross-reference) | One-way Customer indemnity for "every claim" relating to use of the Services; no Vendor indemnity anywhere. Add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity with procedure and remedies; narrow Customer's indemnity to Customer content and breach of Applicable Law. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4) | Mutual cap, but only one month of Fees "actually paid" and "without exception", capping the § 21.3 Excluded Claims. Replace with mutual greater-of 12 months' Fees / USD 1,000,000, Excluded Claims uncapped. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 14.1–14.4 (with §§ 13.2, 15.1) | Meets preferred position; Customer owns Data and Deliverables, Vendor Technology licensed perpetually. No redline. |
| High | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year USD 2M/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights"; conflicts with §§ 7.1, 9.4, 12.3. Delete; Fees due only for Services ordered or used. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 | Sole and exclusive provider for the full term, no category limit, no SLA-failure exit; conflicts with § 12.3. Delete and confirm freedom to source from third parties. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | 24-month post-term, worldwide, "any product or service that competes", no carve-outs; conflicts with § 12.3. Delete. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 13.1 (cf. §§ 13.2–13.3) | Grant revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, excludes Affiliates and contractors, and contradicts §§ 13.2–13.3. Extend to Affiliates/contractors, remove discretionary revocation, cross-reference § 13.3. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4 (with § 13.3) | Customer may assign to Affiliate/successor on notice; Vendor assignment consent-gated; no Vendor rights on our change of control. No redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 9.4 (with §§ 7.3, 24.4, 27.3) | No liquidated damages, penalty or termination fee payable by Customer. Take-or-pay addressed under MINCOMMIT, not double-flagged. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4 | 30 days' notice, whole or part, pro-rata refund, no Vendor convenience right. Tension with § 2.1 raised under MINCOMMIT. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Deviation | § 11.1 (cf. §§ 11.2–11.3) | No transition assistance and immediate permanent deletion of Customer Data. Replace with up to six months' assistance plus export/migration support; deletion per §§ 11.2–11.3. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 (cf. §§ 19.1, 19.4) | 15-day Deliverable warranty that then extinguishes all correction/refund obligations and effectively expires with the § 6.1 acceptance period. Extend to 90 days and confirm it does not limit §§ 19.1 or 19.4. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §§ 22.1–22.3 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, Vendor bears cost below a 5% shortfall. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 | New York law; exclusive New York County courts; no arbitration provision. No redline. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 12.3 (with §§ 7.1, 8.3) | No MFN burdening Customer; § 12.3 confirms none. No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No no-hire or non-solicit covenant; § 12.3 preserves general recruitment hiring. No redline. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §§ 8.2–8.3 | 12-month renewals, 30 days' opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. No redline. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 18.1–18.2 | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp and employer's liability; certificates and notice obligations. Exceeds fallback. No redline. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following seven provisions fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and, in our view, cannot be signed as drafted:

1. **§ 20 — No Vendor indemnity, plus a one-way Customer indemnity for the Services.** No Vendor IP indemnity at all; § 9.3 points to remedies that do not exist.
2. **§ 21.1 — One-month liability cap applied "without exception",** capping indemnities and the other § 21.3 Excluded Claims with no super-cap; the § 1.5 definition of "Fees" excludes the implementation charge, shrinking the base further.
3. **§ 2.1 — Three-year, USD 2M-per-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights.**
4. **§ 2.2 — Full-term sole-and-exclusive sourcing obligation** with no category limit and no performance-based exit.
5. **§ 12.4 — 24-month post-term, worldwide non-compete** covering any competing product or service, including acquisitions, with no carve-outs.
6. **§ 13.1 — Services licence revocable at Vendor's sole discretion** and excluding Affiliates and contractors, with no path to add them; § 13.2 does not cover the hosted Services.
7. **§ 11.1 — Immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data** with no export or migration support.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviations, with the proposals set out in the table above and the playbook fallbacks offered in comments where sensible (12-month reducible commitment with true-up for § 2.1; single product category / 12 months / automatic SLA-failure termination for § 2.2; narrowed named-product covenant for § 12.4; 30–90-day warranty for § 19.2).
2. **Flag the four walk-away clusters** — indemnity, liability cap, commitments/restrictive covenants, and transition — to the business as gating items before further negotiation of commercial terms.
3. **Use the internal inconsistencies as leverage.** § 12.3 already records that we made no exclusivity, non-compete or minimum-volume commitment, and §§ 13.2–13.3 and 11.2–11.3 already contain the language we need; in each case we are asking Vendor to conform the outlier clause to terms it has already accepted elsewhere.
4. **Request an order-of-precedence clause** so that the conflicts among §§ 2.1, 2.2, 9.4, 12.3, 12.4, 13.1 and 11.1 cannot be resolved against us if any of the offending provisions survive.
5. **Repair the § 9.3 cross-reference** to "Section 20.5" as part of the indemnity redline.
6. **Confirm no further review needed** on the eleven compliant items; we do not propose redlines to those provisions, several of which are favourable to us and should be preserved as drafted.
"}
